title: Why Making Your Offer Harder To Buy Raises Quality
hook_text: MAKING IT HARDER TO BUY BRINGS BETTER BUYERS

beats.say: Making something harder to buy can bring better buyers.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a heavy metal vault door closing, dark industrial lighting, low angle.

beats.say: Most sellers think every customer is a good customer.
beats.visual: Wide shot of an empty highway disappearing into a dense gray fog at dusk.

beats.say: How do you filter out the noise and attract people who actually pay?
beats.visual: Low angle of a towering brutalist concrete bridge over dark open water.

beats.say: You add friction to the checkout.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a lone person walking past a single sodium streetlamp on wet asphalt.

beats.say: More steps and strict questions cut your total sign-ups.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a solitary figure standing on a dark ridge line at blue hour.

beats.say: That drop feels terrifying when you need revenue today.
beats.visual: Close-up of heavy rain hitting a dark car window with blurred streetlights behind.

beats.say: Why would anyone want fewer leads knocking on their door?
beats.visual: High angle looking down at an empty multi-lane highway crossing a concrete overpass.

beats.say: Because cheap leads bring endless complaints and refunds.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a worker standing against a massive glowing industrial crane at night.

beats.say: Adding qualifications weeds out the buyers who drain your time.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of heavy steel chains resting on cold wet concrete.

beats.say: The sweet spot is the exact point where volume drops and quality surges.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a massive concrete dam wall under pale moonlight.

beats.say: Build the filter before you scale the traffic.
beats.visual: Wide shot of a single warm practical light cutting through a dark concrete underpass.

beats.say: About 1 in 5 US businesses close in their first year.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a massive empty industrial yard under a cold gray sky.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person walking away down a wet asphalt road toward a single light.

caption: The friction dial changes everything about your customer quality. #moneypsychology #businessrules #entrepreneurship #smartmoney #quietmoney
description: Adding steps and questions to an offer cuts low-quality volume and brings better buyers.
first_comment: What is the hardest friction test you have ever faced as a buyer?

facts.claim: About 1 in 5 US businesses close in their first year
facts.basis: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Business Employment Dynamics

loop_map.stakes: Sellers lose money chasing every low-quality lead that crosses their path.
loop_map.big_question: Why would anyone want fewer leads knocking on their door?
loop_map.assume: More traffic and easier checkout always equal a better business.
loop_map.reveal: Adding friction cuts volume but raises customer quality and retention.
